memory_update.text: KRT is the highest-priority underfollowed public candidate for the restaurant takeout/delivery packaging node because its business is directly tied to single-use disposable products for restaurants and foodservice operators.
GPK and AMCR should be retained as larger reference leaders for paperboard/foodservice packaging and global containers/flexibles/closures scale, but their broader end-market mix reduces node purity.

REYN is a weaker but plausible second-order disposables/tableware candidate; survival to later layers requires proof of restaurant, foodservice, catering, prepared-food, or away-from-home channel exposure.

Important node comparables such as Dart Container, Genpak, Novolex/Eco-Products, and some former Pactiv-style assets appear private or not cleanly US-listed; use them as industry/customer/product benchmarks rather than public candidates in this pass.

Key falsification variables for this node are foodservice revenue mix, pass-through of resin/paper/freight costs, customer concentration, regulatory compliance around plastics/PFAS/compostability, and whether off-premise dining packaging intensity is offset by reuse mandates or packaging reduction.

KRT is the highest-purity underfollowed US-listed small-cap for restaurant disposable packaging, with direct exposure to cups, lids, takeout containers, bags, eco-friendly products, custom printing, chain/distributor accounts, and logistics.
GPK is a mid-cap underfollowed foodservice paperboard packaging candidate; verify the materiality and margins of foodservice/QSR cups, trays, and containers within broader paperboard operations.

AMCR is a reference-scale public packaging name after the Berry Global merger, useful for foodservice cup/container capacity and recyclable/reusable cup context, but less pure due to broad global packaging exposure.

SEE is a second-order foodservice infrastructure candidate via Cryovac/Liquibox packaging for prepared foods, proteins, condiments, and beverages; restaurant exposure is indirect and requires revenue-mix validation.

Pactiv Evergreen would have been a direct public foodservice-packaging reference leader, but it was acquired by Novolex and delisted from Nasdaq on April 1, 2025; treat it as private competitive context, not a current US-listed candidate.

Several highly relevant foodservice packaging competitors are private or non-US-primary-listed, including Dart/Solo, Genpak, Novolex/Pactiv, Huhtamaki, and many custom cup/bag suppliers; this may make the public-market pure-play set unusually narrow.

The strongest chokepoint variables for this node are sustainable/PFAS/plastic compliance, national fulfillment, chain-level custom branding, resin/paper/freight pass-through, food-contact certifications, and ability to supply consistent SKUs across multi-unit restaurant systems.

KRT is the cleanest underfollowed US-listed small-cap candidate for the restaurant takeout/delivery/cold-beverage packaging node, with direct foodservice disposables, compostable product lines, custom branding, and logistics exposure.
GPK should remain in the universe as a mid-cap paperboard foodservice packaging/QSR exposure bridge, but later layers must quantify foodservice mix versus broader consumer-packaging cyclicality.
REYN is a weaker second-order candidate: it has Hefty Tableware and some foodservice/non-retail exposure, but restaurant revenue purity needs verification before it survives beyond Layer 1.

USFD is a distribution-gate candidate rather than a packaging manufacturer; it may matter because restaurant disposables adoption depends on national fulfillment, private-label SKUs, and supplier substitution.
PTVE/Pactiv Evergreen is no longer US-listed after the April 1, 2025 Novolex acquisition and should be treated as a private context anchor or comparable, not an investable public candidate.

Need a later pass for private/context anchors and supplier maps: Novolex/Pactiv, Dart/Solo, WinCup, World Centric, Eco-Products, Amhil, and restaurant distributors may reveal customer dependencies that public filings do not expose.

KRT should be prioritized in later layers as the cleanest small-cap US-listed restaurant packaging/disposables exposure found in this pass; key survival tests are restaurant-chain revenue mix, margin pass-through, customer concentration, and sustainable-product traction.
GPK and AMCR are useful reference anchors for scaled foodservice packaging, but they are less pure and more followed than the preferred underfollowed lane.

PACK remains a speculative-shadow candidate only; include in tracking if evidence emerges that cold-chain or paper-packaging products are being adopted by prepared-food, meal-kit, grocery, or restaurant-adjacent fulfillment customers.

Several strong pure-play restaurant packaging assets appear private or delisted/acquired, including Dart Container, Novolex/Pactiv Evergreen, Anchor Packaging, and Genpak. This scarcity may make the remaining listed exposure more indirect and requires careful mapping.

For this node, the most important next evidence is not generic packaging growth but foodservice-specific customer mix, QSR/coffee chain exposure, compostable/recyclable product economics, input-cost pass-through, and ability to meet national fulfillment/service-level requirements.
